stem: An `incremental` model must carry an enforced contract. Its config currently sets `on_schema_change: ignore` so that unexpected upstream columns are skipped. The contract fails to apply. The team must get the contract enforced while keeping the model incremental. What should they change?

option_texts.A: Set `contract: {enforced: false}` and rely on data tests instead
option_texts.C: Set the materialization to `view` and keep `on_schema_change: ignore`

drill_answer_short: Contracts on incremental models require on_schema_change: append_new_columns or fail
decision_hinge: Models materialized as incremental support model contracts with on_schema_change set to append_new_columns or fail.

plausible_options.B: so that unexpected upstream columns are skipped

A.signal: An `incremental` model must carry an enforced contract
A.requires_fact: To enforce a model's contract, set enforced: true under the contract configuration.

C.signal: The team must get the contract enforced while keeping the model incremental
C.requires_fact: view — views offer support for column names and data types, but not constraints.

distractor_traps.A: T2: data tests check rows after the build; a contract is a build-time guarantee about shape
distractor_traps.B: T3: sync_all_columns is a real on_schema_change value, but contracts accept only append_new_columns or fail
distractor_traps.C: T4: a view carries names and types but not constraints, and the stem requires the model stay incremental

stem: A team adds a `not_null` constraint to a column in a model's YAML, but dbt never submits it to the platform. The model is materialized as `view`, its `contract` is `enforced: true`, and `data_type` is declared for every column. The team must get the constraint applied at the platform level. What is blocking it?

option_texts.A: The YAML declares `data_type` but the contract is not enforced
option_texts.B: The model has no `unique` constraint to anchor the `not_null` one
option_texts.C: The model is a `view`, and constraints need `table` or `incremental`
option_texts.D: The platform treats `not_null` as definable but not enforced

drill_answer_short: Constraints only work on table and incremental models, never on a view
decision_hinge: Constraints only work on table and incremental models. Constraints are never applied on ephemeral models or those materialized as view.

plausible_options.D: dbt never submits it to the platform

A.requires_fact: To use constraints, your model must declare and enforce a contract. This means you need to explicitly define the data_type for every column in your model's schema configuration.

B.signal: A team adds a `not_null` constraint to a column in a model's YAML
B.requires_fact: The structure of a constraint is: type (required): one of not_null, unique, primary_key, foreign_key, check, custom.

distractor_traps.A: T5: right prerequisite, wrong symptom — the stem already states the contract is enforced
distractor_traps.B: T1: there is no rule that a not_null constraint must be anchored by a unique constraint
distractor_traps.D: T3: definable-but-not-enforced is a real platform category, but it would not stop dbt submitting the constraint

stem: A model needs more than one `primary_key` constraint. Because multiple column-level `primary_key` constraints are not supported, those constraints must instead be defined at the ____ level.
decision_hinge: If you define multiple primary_key constraints for a single model, those must be defined at the model level. Defining multiple primary_key constraints at the column level is not supported.

stem: A Snowflake project defines a `primary_key` constraint for documentation purposes. Every run logs a warning that the constraint is not enforced, and the team must silence that warning without removing the constraint or changing the platform. What should they set?

option_texts.D: Set `enforced: false` on the model's contract

drill_answer_short: warn_unenforced: False — the platform supports the constraint but does not enforce it
decision_hinge: Set warn_unenforced to False to skip warnings for constraints that are supported by your platform but not enforced, like primary_key in Snowflake.

plausible_options.A: Every run logs a warning that the constraint is not enforced

C.signal: the team must silence that warning without removing the constraint or changing the platform
C.requires_fact: Adjust its severity or thresholds to warn instead of error.

D.signal: A Snowflake project defines a `primary_key` constraint for documentation purposes
D.requires_fact: To use constraints, your model must declare and enforce a contract.

distractor_traps.A: T3: warn_unsupported silences constraints the platform cannot define at all, such as check in Redshift
distractor_traps.C: T2: severity belongs to tests, not to platform constraints
distractor_traps.D: T4: disabling the contract removes the constraint's prerequisite, which the stem forbids

stem: A versioned model `dim_customers` has `latest_version: 2`, with `v1`, `v2`, and a newly added `v3`. A downstream model uses `ref('dim_customers')` with no version pin, and the team must know which relation it will read. Which version does that ref resolve to?

option_texts.A: Version 1, the oldest one still inside its deprecation window
option_texts.B: Version 2, because it is named by `latest_version`
option_texts.C: Version 3, because a new version overrides `latest_version`
option_texts.D: Version 3, because prerelease versions take precedence

drill_answer_short: v2 — an unpinned ref resolves to whatever latest_version names
decision_hinge: Because v2 is the latest version, it gets some special treatment: it can be defined in a file without a suffix, and ref('dim_customers') will resolve to v2 if a version pin is not specified.

A.requires_fact: Because v2 is the latest version, it gets some special treatment: it can be defined in a file without a suffix, and ref('dim_customers') will resolve to v2 if a version pin is not specified.

D.signal: the team must know which relation it will read
D.requires_fact: A prerelease version 3 is available. It has not yet been marked 'latest' by its maintainer.

distractor_traps.A: T5: v1 stays buildable inside its migration window, but that never makes it the default
distractor_traps.C: T3: the highest number is the prerelease; latest_version is what decides
distractor_traps.D: T1: dbt gives prerelease versions no precedence — it logs that one exists and keeps resolving to latest

stem: A versioned model must follow dbt's standard file-naming convention. `dim_customers` sets `latest_version: 2` and defines v1, v2, and v3. Match each version to the file name dbt expects.
drill_answer_short: Only the latest version may drop the suffix and live in dim_customers.sql
decision_hinge: The prerelease version 3 is defined in dim_customers_v3.sql, the latest version 2 in dim_customers_v2.sql or dim_customers.sql, and version 1 in dim_customers_v1.sql.

stem: A model owner must communicate a timeline for retiring a mature model, so that consumers have a window to migrate. dbt 1.6 introduced first-class support for deprecating models by specifying a ____ property in the model's YAML.
decision_hinge: dbt 1.6 introduced first-class support for deprecating models by specifying a deprecation_date.

stem: A model owner must guarantee that a published model's column names and data types will not change without notice. Only one of the following delivers that guarantee at build time. Accept or reject each option in turn.

option_texts.A: Add a `unique` data test on the model's primary key
option_texts.C: Add a `not_null` column constraint without declaring a contract
option_texts.D: Add the model to a group with `access: public`
option_texts.E: Set `contract: {enforced: true}` with `data_type` on every column

drill_answer_short: An enforced contract with data_type on every column is the build-time guarantee
decision_hinge: To enforce a model's contract, set enforced: true under the contract configuration. When enforced, your contract must include every column's name and data_type.

plausible_options.C: column names and data types will not change without notice

A.signal: Only one of the following delivers that guarantee at build time
A.requires_fact: While building your model, dbt will verify that your model's transformation will produce a dataset matching up with its contract, or it will fail to build.

B.requires_fact: Declaring a deprecation_date for a dbt model provides a mechanism to communicate plans and timelines for long-term support and maintenance.

D.signal: A model owner must guarantee that a published model's column names and data types
D.requires_fact: By default, all models are protected. This means that other models in the same project can reference them, regardless of their group.

distractor_traps.A: T2: a data test checks rows after the build; a contract guarantees the shape at build time
distractor_traps.B: T3: deprecation_date signals a lifecycle end date, not a structural guarantee
distractor_traps.C: T5: right family, wrong completeness — a constraint needs a declared and enforced contract to reach the platform
distractor_traps.D: T3: access controls who may ref the model, not what its columns are
